chapter: Advice to youth and the art of drumming
title: Sticks, rolls and wrist control
summary: He started with heavy sticks, now prefers lighter ones, plays an open roll, and says the secret is in the wrists.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Early drum kits and the gear drummers used

blocks.x: What about sticks? Sticks used to be heavier, it seems.

Yeah, I started out with heavier sticks, and I always compared a drummer with an athlete, with his feet and his legs and arms, muscles and all of this type of thing. As you grow older, you use a much lighter stick because you can't handle that heavy stick anymore, you know. Your wrist, your muscles and things just won't let you do it.
Yeah. I saw a young drummer here a few months ago, in town, a young rock drummer, and he looked
like he was using those oldtime practice sticks.
Yeah, right, yeah, right, right, right and then sometimes, they turn them around and use the butt end, and that's even bigger.
Right. It affects the sounds you get, there's no doubt about that, the weight of the stick.
And certainly, playing shows, whenever I played shows, I'd have to do a lot of rolling, I like a heavier stick, because it's easier to roll.
Right, right, they are, right, right, right.
Do you use an open or a closed roll?

I use a more or less an open roll. I don't use the closed so much, unless I'm going to do something like a solo or something like that, and then I want to close it up and then I want to open it up, or something like that. I do it like that.
But, basically, I use an open roll, a lot.
That -- somebody said -- Buddy Rich, that the best way to practice is just practice a roll, nothing but roll for an hour or two build control in the wrists.
But it'll do that. It's according to

what kind of a roll you're going to do. Right, right. But that is good, because it's in the wrists. You get your wrists supple and everything, and once they're there, relaxed and everything, well, you can do almost anything you want to do.
Yeah, once you get that good, warm feeling in your hands.

Right, right, right, right, right. I was explaining to somebody the other -- not too long ago, they was asking me about the same subject we were talking about on the drums and things, and I said, well, basically the whole secret of it is in your wrists. Because they can tie your arms down and just leave your hands and your wrists open and you can play all the drums you want. You don't have to go up in the air with your sticks and all of that, but you get the same effects that you want with them.
